annotations.text:
A — MENU BAR + PANEL HEADER

Real File / Edit / View / Build / Help menus replace the one
DevDeck dropdown. The panel's two filled buttons become quiet
icon actions, and a filter appears — the tree has outgrown
scrolling.

Keeps the shell model exactly as it is.
Lower risk, smaller change, less distinctive.

B — IDE TOOL WINDOWS

The left edge becomes named tool windows (Project, Git, Agents,
Data). The panel gets a header, its own toolbar and a close.
Adds a run bar and a bottom stripe for Logs / Terminal /
Processes.

More capable and more familiar to anyone who lives in an IDE —
but it moves the shell toward the dockable-panel model your
notes say was removed on purpose.

Both are drawn in DevDeck's own tokens and icons.
B uses the IDE conventions every editor shares —
not any one product's chrome.
